They do look a lot like tie rods! They also both bolt to the knuckle. However, they serve different functions:

The tie rod serves as a ball and socket joint to connect the steering rack with your knuckle, and translates the side-to-side lateral motion of the rack into pivoting, radial motion at the knuckle.

The sway bar (anti-sway bar, stabilizer bar) is a large tube that connects the front left knuckle to the front right knuckle. This promotes stiffer suspension. As you load one corner with weight under turning, the sway bar acts as a counter-force, offsetting the compression of the strut with the rigidity of the bar. This sway bar is connected at each end with sway bar links.

Here's a good picture (not of an Escape unfortunately) showing the setup. The black bellows boot to the right houses the inner tie rod, and the joint connected to it on the left (below the blue knuckle) is the outer tie rod. The rusty black bar starting at top center and ending in the center of the picture is the sway bar, and the silver bar is the sway bar end link. The end links on your Escape look a lot more like tie rods, as there are many different ways to connect the sway bar to the knuckle, with varying stiffness and amounts of play.

To check if the sway bar end links are bad, fully unload the front suspension (wheel off the ground) then grab the sway bar end link and rock it back and forth. If you feel play or hear clunking, you've found your culprit!

In addition to the items /u/Adiabatic mentioned, Escapes frequently develop worn ball joints and/ or torn control arm bushings; either of these things can cause a noise like you describe. You can look at the bushings to see if the rubber is torn or separated from the outer shell of the bushing, checking the ball joints involves jacking up the front wheels to check for movement in the ball joint itself (if you are unsure how to check your ball joints properly, you may wish to have your mechanic do this for you). If either of these things is found to be worn and causing your noise, the usual repair is to replace the entire lower control arm as a complete assembly. They are a common failure part, so aftermarket manufacturers such as Dorman have them available at a very resonable price.

I know this idea is crazy. Maybe I should cross post to /v/crazyideas. On the other hand, what has been done with news aggregators like Voat in the past has not worked, so maybe we need to think about things differently.

Lets look at what happened with Digg and Reddit so far:

  1. Founders form a successful community using Digg's upvote/downvote structure.
  2. The servers start overloading so they need money to keep the lights on when traffic picks up.
  3. The founders take VC money to keep the lights on, and make promises to let the VCs cash out in 5 or 10 years.
  4. People come and make their home for free on the reliable servers paid for by VC money.
  5. The VCs who invested are ready to cash out in 5 or 10 years, so they come in and start pushing for immediate monetization when it comes close to their time to cash out.
  6. Because of the structure of the VC agreements, the VCs can do all kinds of crazy things, like Digg 4.0 or what Reddit is doing now.
  7. The site becomes a ghost town.

What I'm proposing is that Voat gets out ahead of this cycle, by focusing on profits as we grow so VCs don't feel a need to blow the whole thing up to cash out later on.

If Voat puts up ads for the whole site that could create problems, because different communities respond to the same ad in different ways. Think about this:

Lets say Voat puts up a banner ad across the whole site, selling Volkswagen cars. The Volkswagen ads will probably annoy the /v/ford subverse. Volkswagen might not like the /v/ford subverse, either, so they might brigade it. Somebody might pressure somebody else to censor things, or somebody might just accuse Voat of censoring them because they take ads from Volkswagen, even if nobody is censoring anybody. In the end, this hurts Voat and it isn't good for the sponsor, either.

That said, a simple banner ad might work if we had more local, granular control over advertising in our own little communities. Who knows how to advertise to a community better than the moderator of the community? A /v/ford moderator might elect to have ford ads and /v/anticonsumerism might take ads from adbusters magazine. On top of that, while negotiating ads with sponsors, the moderators could make contacts that would help them generate interesting content. I'm sure /v/ford would love to hear from the Ford CEO. What better way to contact him than through Ford's marketing department?

I also don't think the moderators should be forced to handle advertising if they don't want to. Moderators know if their community can and can't handle advertising. Could you imagine having to pitch /v/hailcorporate or /v/conspiracy to marketers? That would be a train wreck. Let the moderators decide for themselves whether they want to advertise or not.

I'm not saying that moderators would necessarily get paid for this work. Maybe they should. Maybe they would get some kind of status as a reward, instead. Maybe the default subverses could be decided by who makes the most money for Voat, I don't know (to be honest, I don't like the idea of default subs). Compensation is a minefield, so I'm not sure I have a good answer to that part of the problem yet.

If it were me, and I owned Voat, and I had to decide right now how to handle compensation, I would probably offer some kind of profit sharing split with the mods, because it's only fair to pay people who work to help you make money. I think it's the right thing to do.

What if the money from the ads corrupts the moderators? If their advertisers pressure moderators to censor their subverses then what?

People will leave the subverse. They won't leave voat, because the advertiser only has that kind of control over the moderator of that one specific subverse, not over the entire voat web site. That's a good thing, because then the problem is in that one specific subverse and not spread across all of voat. People can move from a bad subverse to a good subverse with the click of a mouse. This will exert pressure on the moderators to be fair and not let the advertisers censor their community members.

The drawback to this is that if you are a smaller community you can't command as high a price as if you were a large community. That's why your little wordpress blog can't make as much money as slashdot. Voat could probably make more money per ad if they sold advertising as one big monolithic community, rather than a lot of smaller communities selling ads. That said, the income from a lot of cheaper ads might add up to be worth more to Voat than selling big expensive ads. It would take some experimentation to really know what would be worth more.

The idea is a work in progress. What do you think?
Monetization Idea - Allow Moderators to Make Advertising Decisions

I've done very similar with my S2000 when I rebuilt its engine. It's very important to prime the oil pump as you suggest, as well as changing the oil after the first 5 miles.
